views.name: transactions_cleaned
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  rowid AS transaction_id,
  customer_id,
  -- normalize date: keep only valid ISO dates; SQLite returns NULL for invalid date() parses, so use date() and keep original text when valid
  CASE
    WHEN date(txn_date) IS NOT NULL THEN date(txn_date)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS posted_date,
  -- normalize amount: ensure numeric signed value; try casting txn_amount to numeric, handle NULLs
  CASE
    WHEN txn_amount IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(txn_amount AS NUMERIC)
  END AS amount,
  -- opening_balance_flag: infer if this transaction looks like an opening/beginning balance.
  -- Heuristic: txn_type contains 'opening' or 'begin' (case-insensitive) or txn_amount is zero and txn_type contains 'balance'
  CASE
    WHEN lower(txn_type) LIKE '%opening%' THEN 1
    WHEN lower(txn_type) LIKE '%begin%' THEN 1
    WHEN lower(txn_type) LIKE '%balance%' AND (txn_amount = 0 OR txn_amount IS NULL) THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS opening_balance_flag
FROM customer_transactions
WHERE date(txn_date) IS NOT NULL
views.description: Select and normalize all transaction records: keep only transactions with valid (non-null, parseable) dates; cast/normalize transaction amount to a numeric signed value; identify the customer identifier for each transaction; include transaction posted date and any opening/beginning balance indicator if present.

views.name: calendar_months
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(strftime('%Y', posted_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', posted_date) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  date(date(posted_date, 'start of month'), '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end_date,
  transaction_id
FROM transactions_cleaned
views.description: Generate the full continuous sequence of calendar months (one row per month) covering from the earliest posted_date to the latest posted_date present in transactions_cleaned, with year, month, and month_end_date (last calendar date of that month).

views.name: customer_month_transactions
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  tc.customer_id AS customer_id,
  cm.year AS year,
  cm.month AS month,
  cm.month_end_date AS month_end_date,
  tc.transaction_id AS transaction_id,
  tc.posted_date AS posted_date,
  tc.amount AS amount,
  tc.opening_balance_flag AS opening_balance_flag
FROM
  (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM transactions_cleaned) AS cust
CROSS JOIN
  calendar_months AS cm
LEFT JOIN
  transactions_cleaned AS tc
    ON tc.customer_id = cust.customer_id
    AND tc.posted_date <= cm.month_end_date
views.description: Cross-join all customers present in transactions_cleaned with the calendar_months to produce one row per customer per month, and attach all transactions for that customer with posted_date <= month_end_date (to be used to compute month-end cumulative amounts).

views.name: month_end_balances
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ct.customer_id,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', month_end_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', month_end_date) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  month_end_date,
  -- closing_balance: cumulative sum of txn_amount up to and including this month_end_date per customer
  (SELECT IFNULL(SUM(txn_amount), 0)
   FROM customer_transactions t2
   WHERE t2.customer_id = ct.customer_id
     AND date(t2.txn_date) <= date(ct.month_end_date)
  ) AS closing_balance,
  -- month_over_month_change: difference between this month's closing_balance and prior month's closing_balance per customer
  (
    (SELECT IFNULL(SUM(txn_amount), 0)
     FROM customer_transactions t3
     WHERE t3.customer_id = ct.customer_id
       AND date(t3.txn_date) <= date(ct.month_end_date)
    )
    -
    (SELECT IFNULL(SUM(txn_amount), 0)
     FROM customer_transactions t4
     WHERE t4.customer_id = ct.customer_id
       AND date(t4.txn_date) <= date(date(ct.month_end_date, '-1 month'))
    )
  ) AS month_over_month_change,
  -- bank_cumulative_balance: sum of closing_balance across all customers for that month_end_date
  (SELECT IFNULL(SUM(SumPerCust), 0) FROM (
     SELECT t5.customer_id,
       IFNULL((SELECT SUM(txn_amount) FROM customer_transactions tt
               WHERE tt.customer_id = t5.customer_id
                 AND date(tt.txn_date) <= date(ct.month_end_date)
              ),0) AS SumPerCust
     FROM customer_transactions t5
     GROUP BY t5.customer_id
  )) AS bank_cumulative_balance
FROM
  (
    -- derive distinct customer-month grid from transactions and month-ends
    SELECT DISTINCT
      c.customer_id,
      m.month_end_date
    FROM customer_transactions c
    JOIN (
      SELECT DISTINCT date(txn_date, (strftime('%d', txn_date) || ' days') ) as dummy, date(txn_date) as month_end_date
      FROM customer_transactions
    ) m ON 1=1
  ) ct
views.description: For each customer and month (one row per customer-month), compute the closing_balance as the cumulative sum of that customer's transaction amounts up to and including the month_end_date, carrying forward prior month's closing balance when there are no new transactions, and defaulting to an opening/beginning balance or zero when no prior exists. Also compute month_over_month_change using LAG over customer ordered by year,month, and output bank_cumulative_balance as the sum of closing_balance across all customers for that month.

views.name: transactions_2020_sel
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  rowid AS transaction_id,
  customer_id AS customer_id,
  txn_date AS transaction_date,
  txn_amount AS amount,
  CASE
    WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN 'deposit'
    WHEN txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN 'withdrawal'
    ELSE txn_type
  END AS transaction_type
FROM customer_transactions
WHERE txn_date BETWEEN '2020-01-01' AND '2020-12-31'
views.description: Select all transactions that occur between 2020-01-01 and 2020-12-31 inclusive, keeping transaction date, customer id, amount, and a transaction type indicator (deposit vs withdrawal).

views.name: customer_month_balances_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  substr(txn_date,1,7) AS month,
  SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE 0 END)
    - SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS month_balance
FROM customer_transactions
GROUP BY customer_id, substr(txn_date,1,7)

semantic_filters.month_definition: calendar month of transaction_date (formatted as YYYY-MM)
semantic_filters.aggregation: month_balance = SUM(CASE WHEN transaction_type = 'deposit' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN transaction_type = 'withdrawal' THEN amount ELSE 0 END)

views.description: For each customer and each calendar month in 2020, compute the month-end balance defined as sum(deposits in that month) minus sum(withdrawals in that month). Ensure months with no transactions for a customer are not collapsed here (they will be materialized later); output one row per customer-month present in transactions with the computed balance and month identifier (YYYY-MM).

views.name: all_customers_month_grid
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  m.month
FROM
  (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions) c
CROSS JOIN
  (SELECT '2020-01' AS month UNION ALL
   SELECT '2020-02' UNION ALL
   SELECT '2020-03' UNION ALL
   SELECT '2020-04' UNION ALL
   SELECT '2020-05' UNION ALL
   SELECT '2020-06' UNION ALL
   SELECT '2020-07' UNION ALL
   SELECT '2020-08' UNION ALL
   SELECT '2020-09' UNION ALL
   SELECT '2020-10' UNION ALL
   SELECT '2020-11' UNION ALL
   SELECT '2020-12') m

semantic_filters.cartesian: cross join distinct customers with the 12-month set

views.description: Produce one row for every combination of every customer and each calendar month in 2020 (12 months), so that customers with no transactions in a month have an explicit month row (balance filled in next step).

views.name: customer_month_balances_full
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  g.customer_id AS customer_id,
  g.month AS month,
  COALESCE(a.month_balance, 0) AS month_balance,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(a.month_balance, 0) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS positive_flag
FROM
  all_customers_month_grid g
LEFT JOIN
  customer_month_balances_agg a
ON
  g.customer_id = a.customer_id
  AND g.month = a.month

semantic_filters.join: left join all_customers_month_grid to customer_month_balances_agg on (customer_id, month)

views.description: Left-join the all-customers-month grid to the per-customer-month aggregated balances to produce one row per customer-month for all customers and all 2020 months, filling missing balances with zero; also produce a positive_flag indicating month_balance > 0.

views.name: transactions_monthly_norm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_transactions.customer_id AS customer_id,
  rowid AS transaction_id,
  substr(txn_date, 1, 7) || '-01' AS month_start_date,
  CASE LOWER(txn_type)
    WHEN 'deposit' THEN ABS(txn_amount)
    WHEN 'withdrawal' THEN -ABS(txn_amount)
    ELSE txn_amount
  END AS signed_amount,
  txn_date AS transaction_date
FROM customer_transactions
views.description: Normalize raw transactions by mapping each transaction date to the first day of its month and signing amounts so deposits are positive and withdrawals are negative. Keep one row per original transaction with month and customer identifiers.

views.name: monthly_net_per_customer
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ct.customer_id AS customer_id,
  substr(ct.txn_date, 1, 7) || '-01' AS month_start_date,
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN ct.txn_type = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount
      WHEN ct.txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN -ct.txn_amount
      ELSE ct.txn_amount
    END
  ) AS monthly_net
FROM customer_transactions ct
GROUP BY ct.customer_id, month_start_date
views.description: Aggregate normalized transactions to compute the monthly net amount per customer-month by summing signed amounts.

views.name: monthly_closing_balance_per_customer
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.customer_id AS customer_id,
  m.month_start_date AS month_start_date,
  COALESCE(n.monthly_net, 0) AS monthly_net,
  SUM(COALESCE(n2.monthly_net, 0)) OVER (
    PARTITION BY m.customer_id
    ORDER BY m.month_start_date
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS closing_balance
FROM
  -- base grid of customer-months comes from monthly_net_per_customer if available;
  -- to ensure every customer-month that has a monthly_net is included, start from that view.
  monthly_net_per_customer AS m
LEFT JOIN monthly_net_per_customer AS n
  ON n.customer_id = m.customer_id
  AND n.month_start_date = m.month_start_date
LEFT JOIN monthly_net_per_customer AS n2
  ON n2.customer_id = m.customer_id
  AND n2.month_start_date IS NOT NULL
views.description: Compute each customer-month's closing balance as the cumulative sum (running total) of that customer's monthly_net ordered by month ascending.

views.name: most_recent_and_prior_growth_per_customer
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.customer_id AS customer_id,
  -- prior month start date (the month immediately before the most recent month for this customer)
  prior.month_start_date AS prior_month_start_date,
  prior.closing_balance AS prior_closing_balance,
  recent.month_start_date AS recent_month_start_date,
  recent.closing_balance AS recent_closing_balance,
  CASE
    WHEN prior.closing_balance IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN prior.closing_balance != 0 THEN (recent.closing_balance - prior.closing_balance) * 1.0 / prior.closing_balance
    ELSE recent.closing_balance * 100.0
  END AS growth_rate
FROM (
  -- identify, per customer, the most recent month_start_date they have a closing_balance
  SELECT customer_id, MAX(month_start_date) AS recent_month_start_date
  FROM monthly_closing_balance_per_customer
  GROUP BY customer_id
) m
JOIN monthly_closing_balance_per_customer recent
  ON recent.customer_id = m.customer_id
  AND recent.month_start_date = m.recent_month_start_date
JOIN monthly_closing_balance_per_customer prior
  ON prior.customer_id = m.customer_id
  AND prior.month_start_date = (
    -- pick the immediately prior month_start_date for this customer
    SELECT MAX(month_start_date)
    FROM monthly_closing_balance_per_customer pc
    WHERE pc.customer_id = m.customer_id
      AND pc.month_start_date < m.recent_month_start_date
  )
views.description: For each customer, identify the most recent month and the immediately prior month (exclude customers without a prior month), bring their closing balances together, and compute the growth rate as defined (if prior balance != 0 use (recent - prior)/prior else growth = recent * 100). One row per customer that has at least two months.

views.name: daily_balances_on_first_of_month
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id AS user_id,
  amount AS balance_amount,
  posted_date AS snapshot_date,
  substr(posted_date, 1, 7) AS month_of_snapshot
FROM
  transactions_cleaned
WHERE
  -- keep only snapshots that fall on the first day of a month (ISO YYYY-MM-DD or similar)
  substr(posted_date, 9, 2) = '01'
views.description: Select balance snapshot records that fall exactly on the first day of each month (the measured balance for a user on that date). This is a row-level cohort of all user balance observations that are timestamped on month-first dates and will be the raw source for monthly aggregation.

views.name: monthly_user_balance
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.user_id AS user_id,
  date(substr(d.snapshot_date,1,10) || '','start of month') AS month,
  d.balance_amount AS user_balance_on_month_first
FROM daily_balances_on_first_of_month d
views.description: For each user and for each month (represented by the first-day snapshot), produce that user's balance as of the first day of the month. Aggregation here ensures one row per user per month (if multiple snapshots on the same day exist, resolve by taking the last/representative value in later alignment step).

views.name: monthly_previous_month_report
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  printf('%04d-%02d', calendar_year, month_number) AS month_m,
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(prev_month_totals.prev_total, 0) < 0 THEN 0
    ELSE COALESCE(prev_month_totals.prev_total, 0)
  END AS previous_month_total_balance
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT calendar_year, month_number
  FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
) months
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    calendar_year AS yr,
    month_number AS mn,
    SUM(sales) AS month_total
  FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
  GROUP BY calendar_year, month_number
) month_totals
  ON month_totals.yr = months.calendar_year AND month_totals.mn = months.month_number
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    mt_next.calendar_year AS next_year,
    mt_next.month_number AS next_month,
    COALESCE(mt_prev.month_total, 0) AS prev_total
  FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT calendar_year, month_number
    FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
  ) mt_next
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
      calendar_year,
      month_number,
      SUM(sales) AS month_total
    FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
    GROUP BY calendar_year, month_number
  ) mt_prev
  ON (
    (mt_prev.calendar_year = mt_next.calendar_year AND mt_prev.month_number = mt_next.month_number - 1)
    OR
    (mt_prev.calendar_year = mt_next.calendar_year - 1 AND mt_prev.month_number = 12 AND mt_next.month_number = 1)
  )
) prev_month_totals
  ON prev_month_totals.next_year = months.calendar_year AND prev_month_totals.next_month = months.month_number
views.description: For each target month M (every month except the earliest present), join the prior month's total (month P = month immediately before M) to M, replace any negative total with zero, and produce one row per month M with the non-negative previous_month_total_balance. Order of months is chronological (ordering applied at final query).

views.name: raw_customer_transactions
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id AS customer_id,
  txn_date   AS tx_date,
  txn_amount AS amount,
  txn_type   AS tx_type,
  rowid      AS transaction_id
FROM customer_transactions
views.description: Select raw transaction rows needed: customer identifier, transaction date (calendar date), transaction amount, and transaction type. This is the input cohort of all transactions used to compute per-day net amounts.

views.name: daily_net_balance
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  txn_date AS date,
  SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END) AS daily_net_balance,
  substr(min(txn_date) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id), 1, 7) AS first_activity_month
FROM customer_transactions
GROUP BY customer_id, txn_date
views.description: Aggregate transactions to compute each customer's per-day net balance where deposit-type transactions add and all other types subtract. One row per customer-date with the summed daily balance. Also compute each customer's first_activity_month (year-month of their earliest transaction) for later filtering.

views.name: customer_day_30day_avg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.customer_id,
  d.date,
  -- 30-day rolling average of daily_net_balance including current day, only when full 30-day window exists
  CASE
    WHEN COUNT(d2.daily_net_balance) = 30 THEN
      MAX(0, AVG(d2.daily_net_balance))
    ELSE NULL
  END AS avg_30day_nonnegative
FROM
  daily_net_balance d
JOIN
  daily_net_balance d2
  ON d.customer_id = d2.customer_id
  AND d2.date <= d.date
  AND d2.date > date(d.date, '-30 days')
GROUP BY
  d.customer_id,
  d.date
HAVING
  COUNT(d2.daily_net_balance) >= 30
views.description: For each customer-day, compute the 30-day rolling average of the daily_net_balance using only full 30-day windows (i.e., produce a value only when there are at least 30 days of daily_net_balance up to and including that day). Replace any negative rolling-average values with zero (i.e., apply max(rolling_avg, 0)).

views.name: monthly_customer_max_30day_and_monthly_totals
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cmb.customer_id AS customer_id,
  cmb.month AS month,
  -- per customer-month: maximum avg_30day_nonnegative for that customer's days in the month,
  -- computed by joining customer_day_30day_avg on customer_id and date within month
  MAX(cd.avg_30day_nonnegative) AS customer_month_max_30day,
  -- month total: sum of the per-customer monthly maxima across customers for that month
  SUM(MAX(cd.avg_30day_nonnegative)) OVER (PARTITION BY cmb.month) AS month_total_max_30day_avg_balance
FROM
  -- base grid of customers x months to ensure even months with no days are represented
  all_customers_month_grid AS cmb
LEFT JOIN
  -- daily per-customer 30-day averages (has date)
  customer_day_30day_avg AS cd
  ON cd.customer_id = cmb.customer_id
  -- join days that fall in the calendar month represented by cmb.month
  AND strftime('%Y-%m', cd.date) = strftime('%Y-%m', cmb.month)
-- Exclude a customer's first_activity_month from contributing: filter out rows where date's month = first_activity_month
LEFT JOIN
  daily_net_balance AS dnb
  ON dnb.customer_id = cd.customer_id
  AND strftime('%Y-%m', dnb.date) = strftime('%Y-%m', cd.date)
WHERE
  NOT (dnb.first_activity_month IS NOT NULL AND strftime('%Y-%m', cd.date) = strftime('%Y-%m', dnb.first_activity_month))
GROUP BY
  cmb.month,
  cmb.customer_id
views.description: For each calendar month and customer (excluding the customer's first_activity_month), take the maximum avg_30day_nonnegative for that customer's days falling in the month. Then aggregate (sum) those per-customer monthly maxima across all customers to produce one row per month with the month_total_max_30day_avg_balance.

views.name: transactions_by_customer_date
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  txn_date AS date,
  SUM(txn_amount) AS daily_delta
FROM customer_transactions
GROUP BY customer_id, txn_date
views.description: All raw transaction events normalized to one row per customer-date with that date's net balance change (e.g. sum of transactions posted that day).  This is the base set of dated balance deltas per customer.

views.name: customer_date_range
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  MIN(txn_date) AS min_date,
  MAX(txn_date) AS max_date
FROM customer_transactions
GROUP BY customer_id
views.description: For each customer, the earliest and latest transaction dates (their inclusive active date range).

views.name: customer_all_dates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  date(txn_date) AS date
FROM (
  SELECT
    ct.customer_id,
    date(ct.min_txn, '+' || tens.i*10000 + hundreds.i*1000 + tens_th.i*100 + tens_h.i*10 + ones.i || ' days') AS txn_date
  FROM (
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      MIN(date(txn_date)) AS min_txn,
      MAX(date(txn_date)) AS max_txn,
      julianday(MAX(date(txn_date))) - julianday(MIN(date(txn_date))) AS span_days
    FROM customer_transactions
    GROUP BY customer_id
  ) ct
  JOIN (
    SELECT 0 AS i UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4
    UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9
  ) ones
  JOIN (
    SELECT 0 AS i UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4
    UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9
  ) tens_h
  JOIN (
    SELECT 0 AS i UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4
    UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9
  ) tens_th
  JOIN (
    SELECT 0 AS i UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4
    UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9
  ) hundreds
  JOIN (
    SELECT 0 AS i UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4
    UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9
  ) tens
  WHERE (tens.i*10000 + hundreds.i*1000 + tens_th.i*100 + tens_h.i*10 + ones.i) <= ct.span_days
)
WHERE date(txn_date) BETWEEN (SELECT MIN(date(txn_date)) FROM customer_transactions WHERE customer_id = customer_id)
                         AND (SELECT MAX(date(txn_date)) FROM customer_transactions WHERE customer_id = customer_id)
views.description: For each customer, every calendar date in the inclusive range from their earliest to latest transaction date (one row per customer-date).

views.name: raw_event_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- event_id: synthesize a unique id per original event by combining visit_id and sequence_number
  visit_id || '-' || CAST(sequence_number AS TEXT) AS event_id,
  event_type,
  ph.product_id AS product_id,
  events.page_id AS page_id,
  su.user_id AS user_id,
  events.event_time AS timestamp,
  events.visit_id AS session_id,
  NULL AS quantity,
  json_object(
    'cookie_id', events.cookie_id,
    'event_name_lookup', (SELECT event_name FROM shopping_cart_event_identifier ei WHERE ei.event_type = events.event_type LIMIT 1),
    'page_name', ph.page_name
  ) AS other_event_metadata
FROM shopping_cart_events AS events
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_page_hierarchy AS ph
  ON events.page_id = ph.page_id
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_users AS su
  ON events.cookie_id = su.cookie_id
WHERE events.page_id NOT IN (1, 2, 12, 13)
views.description: Select the raw event rows of interest from event/activity logs (page views, add-to-cart events, purchase events, and any cart-state events) after applying the page-id exclusion filter. Do not aggregate; keep one row per original event.

views.name: product_event_types
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- preserve original event identifier as the event_id (grain)
  shopping_cart_events.rowid AS event_id,
  -- prefer product_id from events' page hierarchy when available, else use event-level product_id if present
  COALESCE(shopping_cart_page_hierarchy.product_id, shopping_cart_events.page_id * 0.0 + shopping_cart_page_hierarchy.product_id) AS product_id,
  -- canonicalize event types by joining to identifier table and mapping known names to a small set
  CASE
    WHEN lower(shopping_cart_event_identifier.event_name) = lower('Page View') THEN 'view'
    WHEN lower(shopping_cart_event_identifier.event_name) = lower('Add to Cart') THEN 'add_to_cart'
    WHEN lower(shopping_cart_event_identifier.event_name) IN (lower('Checkout'), lower('Purchase')) THEN 'purchase'
    ELSE
      CASE
        -- fallback mapping by numeric event_type if event_name missing
        WHEN shopping_cart_events.event_type = shopping_cart_event_identifier.event_type THEN
          CASE
            WHEN lower(shopping_cart_event_identifier.event_name) = lower('Page View') THEN 'view'
            WHEN lower(shopping_cart_event_identifier.event_name) = lower('Add to Cart') THEN 'add_to_cart'
            ELSE 'cart_state'
          END
        ELSE 'cart_state'
      END
  END AS event_type_canonical,
  -- ensure timestamp is present and use the events table timestamp
  shopping_cart_events.event_time AS timestamp,
  -- map user/session ids to requested names
  shopping_cart_events.cookie_id AS user_id,
  shopping_cart_events.visit_id AS session_id,
  -- ensure quantity exists; default to 1 for view/add if missing
  COALESCE(shopping_cart_events.sequence_number * 0 + shopping_cart_page_hierarchy.product_id * 0 + NULL, 1) AS quantity
FROM shopping_cart_events
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_event_identifier
  ON shopping_cart_events.event_type = shopping_cart_event_identifier.event_type
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_page_hierarchy
  ON shopping_cart_events.page_id = shopping_cart_page_hierarchy.page_id
views.description: Normalize and canonicalize event rows into a consistent set of event_type categories (e.g., 'view', 'add_to_cart', 'purchase', 'cart_state') and ensure product identifier and timestamp are present and consistent. Keep one row per original event.

views.name: left_in_cart_flags
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  add_events.rowid AS add_event_id,
  add_events.page_id AS product_id,
  shopping_cart_users.user_id AS user_id,
  add_events.visit_id AS session_id,
  add_events.event_time AS timestamp_add,
  CASE
    WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM shopping_cart_events later_evt
      WHERE later_evt.cookie_id = add_events.cookie_id
        AND later_evt.visit_id = add_events.visit_id
        AND later_evt.page_id = add_events.page_id
        AND later_evt.event_time > add_events.event_time
        AND later_evt.event_type = 2
    ) THEN 0
    WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM shopping_cart_events later_evt2
      WHERE later_evt2.cookie_id = add_events.cookie_id
        AND later_evt2.page_id = add_events.page_id
        AND later_evt2.event_time > add_events.event_time
        AND later_evt2.event_type = 2
    ) THEN 0
    ELSE 1
  END AS left_in_cart_flag
FROM shopping_cart_events AS add_events
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_users
  ON add_events.cookie_id = shopping_cart_users.cookie_id
WHERE add_events.event_type = 1
views.description: For each add-to-cart event (at the event granularity), determine whether that added item was later purchased by the same user/session for the same product (i.e., mark add events that remained in cart without a subsequent purchase). Keep one row per add-to-cart event with a boolean flag left_in_cart.

views.name: monthly_interest_records_sel
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  rowid AS record_id,
  interest_id,
  (SELECT interest_name FROM interest_map im WHERE im.id = interest_metrics.interest_id) AS interest_name,
  date(substr(month_year,4,4) || '-' || substr(month_year,1,2) || '-01') AS record_month,
  composition,
  index_value AS "index"
FROM interest_metrics
WHERE
  month_year BETWEEN '09-2018' AND '08-2019'
  AND index_value IS NOT NULL
  AND index_value != 0
views.description: Select all raw records restricted to the target date range (2018-09 through 2019-08 inclusive) and exclude records with null or zero index. Keep the record-level fields needed to compute (composition / index), the interest identifier and interest name, and the record date truncated to the calendar month.

views.name: monthly_interest_index_composition_norm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  mir.record_id AS record_id,
  mir.interest_id AS interest_id,
  mir.interest_name AS interest_name,
  mir.record_month AS record_month,
  CASE
    WHEN CAST(mir."index" AS REAL) = 0 OR mir."index" IS NULL OR mir.composition IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(mir.composition AS REAL) / CAST(mir."index" AS REAL)
  END AS index_composition
FROM monthly_interest_records_sel AS mir
views.description: For each record, compute the per-record metric index_composition = composition / index (with appropriate numeric cast/handling). Keep the same record-level grain with the computed metric and canonical month value.

views.name: monthly_interest_avg_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  mir.record_month AS record_month,
  mir.interest_id AS interest_id,
  mir.interest_name AS interest_name,
  AVG(mir.index_composition) AS avg_index_composition
FROM monthly_interest_index_composition_norm AS mir
GROUP BY
  mir.record_month,
  mir.interest_id,
  mir.interest_name
views.description: For each month and each interest, compute the average of index_composition across that interest's records in that month. This yields one row per interest per month with the month's average index_composition.

views.name: monthly_top_interest_and_3mo_rollup
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  avg_by_month.record_month AS date,
  avg_by_month.interest_name AS interest_name,
  avg_by_month.avg_index_composition AS max_index_composition,
  -- 3-month rolling average of the month's top avg_index_composition using current and two prior months
  CASE
    WHEN prev2.max_index_composition IS NOT NULL AND prev1.max_index_composition IS NOT NULL THEN
      (avg_by_month.avg_index_composition + prev1.max_index_composition + prev2.max_index_composition) / 3.0
    ELSE NULL
  END AS rolling_avg_max_index_composition_3mo,
  prev1.interest_name AS prev_1_month_interest_name,
  prev1.max_index_composition AS prev_1_month_max_index_composition,
  prev2.interest_name AS prev_2_month_interest_name,
  prev2.max_index_composition AS prev_2_month_max_index_composition
FROM (
  -- For each month, pick the single top interest by avg_index_composition; ties broken by lexicographically smallest interest_name
  SELECT
    m.record_month,
    m.interest_id,
    m.interest_name,
    m.avg_index_composition
  FROM monthly_interest_avg_agg m
  JOIN (
    -- determine the max avg_index_composition per month
    SELECT
      record_month,
      MAX(avg_index_composition) AS max_avg_index_composition
    FROM monthly_interest_avg_agg
    GROUP BY record_month
  ) mm
  ON m.record_month = mm.record_month
     AND m.avg_index_composition = mm.max_avg_index_composition
  -- tie-breaker: pick lexicographically smallest interest_name when multiple have same max value
  WHERE m.interest_name = (
    SELECT MIN(m2.interest_name)
    FROM monthly_interest_avg_agg m2
    WHERE m2.record_month = m.record_month
      AND m2.avg_index_composition = m.avg_index_composition
  )
) AS avg_by_month
LEFT JOIN (
  -- previous 1 month top interest
  SELECT
    record_month AS record_month_plus1,
    interest_name,
    avg_index_composition AS max_index_composition
  FROM (
    SELECT
      m.record_month,
      m.interest_name,
      m.avg_index_composition
    FROM monthly_interest_avg_agg m
    JOIN (
      SELECT
        record_month,
        MAX(avg_index_composition) AS max_avg_index_composition
      FROM monthly_interest_avg_agg
      GROUP BY record_month
    ) mm ON m.record_month = mm.record_month
           AND m.avg_index_composition = mm.max_avg_index_composition
    WHERE m.interest_name = (
      SELECT MIN(m2.interest_name)
      FROM monthly_interest_avg_agg m2
      WHERE m2.record_month = m.record_month
        AND m2.avg_index_composition = m.avg_index_composition
    )
  )
) AS prev1
ON prev1.record_month_plus1 = (
  -- compute prior month string by naive string manipulation assuming record_month in YYYY-MM or similar sortable format
  -- we join by taking the immediate prior month: convert YYYY-MM to yyyy*100+mm integer then subtract 1 and format back
  substr(avg_by_month.record_month,1,4) || '-' ||
  printf('%02d',
    (CAST(substr(avg_by_month.record_month,6,2) AS INTEGER) - 1)
    + 0
  )
)
LEFT JOIN (
  -- previous 2 months top interest
  SELECT
    record_month AS record_month_plus2,
    interest_name,
    avg_index_composition AS max_index_composition
  FROM (
    SELECT
      m.record_month,
      m.interest_name,
      m.avg_index_composition
    FROM monthly_interest_avg_agg m
    JOIN (
      SELECT
        record_month,
        MAX(avg_index_composition) AS max_avg_index_composition
      FROM monthly_interest_avg_agg
      GROUP BY record_month
    ) mm ON m.record_month = mm.record_month
           AND m.avg_index_composition = mm.max_avg_index_composition
    WHERE m.interest_name = (
      SELECT MIN(m2.interest_name)
      FROM monthly_interest_avg_agg m2
      WHERE m2.record_month = m.record_month
        AND m2.avg_index_composition = m.avg_index_composition
    )
  )
) AS prev2
ON prev2.record_month_plus2 = (
  substr(avg_by_month.record_month,1,4) || '-' ||
  printf('%02d',
    (CAST(substr(avg_by_month.record_month,6,2) AS INTEGER) - 2)
    + 0
  )
)
views.description: From the per-month-per-interest averages, pick the single top interest for each month (highest avg_index_composition; break ties deterministically by lexicographically smallest interest_name). Then compute a 3-month rolling average of that month's top avg_index_composition using the current and two prior months (result null if fewer than 3 months available). Also attach the top-interest names and avg values for the 1-month-prior and 2-months-prior months for each month row.

views.name: raw_compositions
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  interest_metrics.interest_id AS interest_id,
  interest_map.interest_name AS interest_name,
  CAST(interest_metrics._month AS INTEGER) AS month,
  interest_metrics.composition AS composition_value
FROM interest_metrics
JOIN interest_map
  ON interest_metrics.interest_id = interest_map.id
WHERE interest_metrics.composition IS NOT NULL
views.description: Select all raw monthly composition records for interests, excluding rows where the composition value is NULL or missing.

views.name: normalized_compositions
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  im.id AS interest_id,
  im.interest_name AS interest_name,
  -- normalize month: prefer interest_metrics.month_year if available, else construct from _year and _month
  CASE
    WHEN trim(coalesce(imt.month_year, '')) <> '' THEN imt.month_year
    WHEN imt._year IS NOT NULL AND imt._month IS NOT NULL
      THEN printf('%02d-%d', CAST(imt._month AS INTEGER), CAST(imt._year AS INTEGER))
    WHEN imt._year IS NOT NULL THEN CAST(CAST(imt._year AS INTEGER) AS TEXT)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS month_normalized,
  -- ensure composition is numeric: prefer interest_metrics.composition, fallback NULL
  CASE
    WHEN imt.composition IS NOT NULL THEN imt.composition
    ELSE NULL
  END AS composition_value_numeric
FROM interest_map im
LEFT JOIN interest_metrics imt
  ON CAST(im.id AS REAL) = imt.interest_id
views.description: Clean and canonicalize the raw composition fields: ensure month is a proper date or year-month token, ensure composition_value is numeric, and propagate interest name for each interest_id.

views.name: interest_max_by_month
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  nc.interest_id AS interest_id,
  im.interest_name AS interest_name,
  nc.month_normalized AS month_normalized,
  nc.composition_value_numeric AS composition_value_numeric,
  mx.max_composition_value AS max_composition_value
FROM normalized_compositions nc
JOIN (
  SELECT
    interest_id,
    MAX(composition_value_numeric) AS max_composition_value
  FROM normalized_compositions
  GROUP BY interest_id
) mx
  ON nc.interest_id = mx.interest_id
  AND nc.composition_value_numeric = mx.max_composition_value
LEFT JOIN interest_map im
  ON im.id = nc.interest_id
views.description: For each interest, find the maximum composition value across all months and retain the month(s) where that maximum occurs (one row per interest per maximal-month).

views.name: ranked_interest_maxima
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  im.id AS interest_id,
  im.interest_name AS interest_name,
  imb.month_normalized AS month_normalized,
  imb.max_composition_value AS max_composition_value,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY imb.max_composition_value DESC) AS rank_desc,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY imb.max_composition_value ASC) AS rank_asc
FROM interest_map im
JOIN interest_max_by_month imb
  ON im.id = imb.interest_id
views.description: Rank interests by their maximum composition value so top and bottom interests can be selected. Keep one representative row per interest (if multiple months tied, any one is acceptable).

views.name: region_year_transactions
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  bt.txn_id AS transaction_id,
  COALESCE(bm.region, '') AS region,
  -- extract 4-digit year from txn_time (ISO 8601) if present, else try txn_date formatted as DD-MM-YYYY
  COALESCE(
    CASE
      WHEN length(bt.txn_time) >= 4 AND instr(bt.txn_time, '-') = 0 THEN substr(bt.txn_time, 1, 4)
      WHEN instr(bt.txn_time, 'T') > 0 THEN substr(bt.txn_time, 1, 4)
      WHEN instr(bt.txn_date, '-') > 0 AND length(bt.txn_date) >= 4 THEN substr(bt.txn_date, -4, 4)
      ELSE NULL
    END,
    ''
  ) AS year,
  -- dollars_spent: compute dollars for BUY transactions as quantity * price on matching date; if price missing, NULL
  -- Join to bitcoin_prices on ticker and market_date matching txn_date (both stored as TEXT DD-MM-YYYY)
  -- Use NULL for dollars_spent when quantity or price is NULL
  (CASE
     WHEN bt.quantity IS NULL THEN NULL
     WHEN bp.price IS NULL THEN NULL
     ELSE bt.quantity * bp.price
   END) AS dollars_spent,
  -- bitcoin_quantity: preserve quantity (explicit NULL if missing)
  bt.quantity AS bitcoin_quantity
FROM bitcoin_transactions bt
LEFT JOIN bitcoin_members bm
  ON bt.member_id = bm.member_id
LEFT JOIN bitcoin_prices bp
  ON bp.ticker = bt.ticker
  AND bp.market_date = bt.txn_date
views.description: Select and normalize transaction-level records that include region, year, dollar amount spent, and bitcoin quantity purchased; apply basic cleaning to ensure nullability is explicit (but do not apply the question's exclusion filters yet).

views.name: region_year_totals
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cr.region_name AS region,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', bt.txn_time) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  SUM(ct.txn_amount) AS total_dollars_spent,
  SUM(bt.quantity) AS total_bitcoin_quantity
FROM customer_regions cr
LEFT JOIN bitcoin_members bm
  ON bm.region = cr.region_name
LEFT JOIN bitcoin_transactions bt
  ON bt.member_id = bm.member_id
LEFT JOIN customer_transactions ct
  ON ct.customer_id = cr.region_id
GROUP BY
  cr.region_name,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', bt.txn_time) AS INTEGER)
views.description: Aggregate totals per region and year: sum of dollars spent and sum of bitcoin quantity purchased. Keep one row per region-year with both totals (totals may be null if input nulls exist).

views.name: region_first_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  region,
  MIN(calendar_year) AS first_year_for_region
FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
GROUP BY region
views.description: Determine the earliest year present for each region (one row per region) so that that year can be excluded later.

views.name: region_year_price_and_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ryt.year AS year,
  ryt.region AS region,
  (ryt.total_dollars_spent / NULLIF(ryt.total_bitcoin_quantity,0)) AS average_purchase_price_per_bitcoin,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ryt.year ORDER BY (ryt.total_dollars_spent / NULLIF(ryt.total_bitcoin_quantity,0)) DESC) AS region_year_rank_by_average_price,
  ((ryt.total_dollars_spent / NULLIF(ryt.total_bitcoin_quantity,0)) - (prev.total_dollars_spent / NULLIF(prev.total_bitcoin_quantity,0)))
    / NULLIF((prev.total_dollars_spent / NULLIF(prev.total_bitcoin_quantity,0)), 0) AS percent_change_from_previous_year
FROM region_year_totals ryt
LEFT JOIN region_first_year rfy
  ON ryt.region = rfy.region
LEFT JOIN region_year_totals prev
  ON ryt.region = prev.region
  AND prev.year = ryt.year - 1
WHERE
  -- exclude each region's first year
  ryt.year IS NOT NULL
  AND (rfy.first_year_for_region IS NULL OR ryt.year <> rfy.first_year_for_region)
  -- exclude rows where totals are null or bitcoin quantity = 0
  AND ryt.total_dollars_spent IS NOT NULL
  AND ryt.total_bitcoin_quantity IS NOT NULL
  AND ryt.total_bitcoin_quantity <> 0
views.description: For region-year rows (excluding each region's first year and excluding rows where totals are null or bitcoin quantity = 0), compute the average purchase price per bitcoin (total_dollars_spent / total_bitcoin_quantity), compute the year-over-year percent change in that average price for the same region (relative to the previous year), and within each year rank regions by the average price.

views.name: raw_rows_in_date_range
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ticker AS ticker,
  market_date AS date,
  volume AS raw_volume_string
FROM bitcoin_prices
WHERE market_date IS NOT NULL
views.description: Select bitcoin_prices rows restricted to the target date range (only rows whose date is within the requested window). Do not change or parse volume strings here — just filter by date and keep raw fields needed (ticker, date, raw_volume_string, and any row id/ordering if present).

views.name: parsed_volume
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ticker,
  market_date AS date,
  CASE
    WHEN volume IS NULL OR trim(volume) = '-' THEN 0.0
    ELSE
      -- remove any surrounding spaces
      (
        CASE
          WHEN substr(trim(volume), -1, 1) = 'K' THEN
            CAST(replace(substr(trim(volume), 1, length(trim(volume)) - 1), ',', '') AS REAL) * 1000.0
          WHEN substr(trim(volume), -1, 1) = 'M' THEN
            CAST(replace(substr(trim(volume), 1, length(trim(volume)) - 1), ',', '') AS REAL) * 1000000.0
          ELSE
            CAST(replace(trim(volume), ',', '') AS REAL)
        END
      )
  END AS volume
FROM bitcoin_prices
views.description: Normalize/parse the raw volume string into a numeric volume: treat '-' as 0, if ending with 'K' multiply numeric prefix by 1,000, if ending with 'M' multiply numeric prefix by 1,000,000, otherwise cast the numeric string as-is. Emit the parsed numeric volume alongside the original keys.

views.name: previous_non_zero_volume_per_row
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.ticker AS ticker,
  p.date AS date,
  p.volume AS volume,
  (
    SELECT pv.volume
    FROM parsed_volume pv
    WHERE pv.ticker = p.ticker
      AND pv.date < p.date
      AND pv.volume > 0
    ORDER BY pv.date DESC
    LIMIT 1
  ) AS previous_non_zero_volume
FROM parsed_volume p
views.description: For each row (one per ticker+date) compute the most recent earlier date's parsed volume for the same ticker that is > 0. This is a backward-looking analytic: find the previous row by date with volume > 0 and return its numeric volume; if none exists return null.

views.name: compute_percent_change_and_filter_range
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.ticker AS ticker,
  p.date AS date,
  p.volume AS volume,
  w.previous_non_zero_volume AS previous_non_zero_volume,
  CASE
    WHEN w.previous_non_zero_volume IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE (p.volume - w.previous_non_zero_volume) / w.previous_non_zero_volume * 100.0
  END AS percent_change
FROM parsed_volume p
LEFT JOIN previous_non_zero_volume_per_row w
  ON p.ticker = w.ticker
  AND p.date = w.date
views.description: From the rows with parsed volume and previous_non_zero_volume computed, produce final rows only for dates within the requested window, include ticker, date, volume, previous_non_zero_volume, and percent_change computed as (volume - previous_non_zero_volume) / previous_non_zero_volume * 100; if previous_non_zero_volume is null then percent_change is null. This step also enforces final ordering (ticker ASC, date ASC).

views.name: raw_items_with_loss_rate
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  item_code AS item_id,
  "loss_rate_%" AS loss_rate_raw
FROM
  veg_loss_rate_df
WHERE
  "loss_rate_%" IS NOT NULL
views.description: Select all rows representing 'items' in the veg-whsle data that have a non-null loss rate field; keep the original loss rate value and any item identifier. This step does not perform type coercion, only filters out rows missing the loss rate.

views.name: clean_numeric_loss_rates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  item_id,
  CASE
    WHEN trim(loss_rate_raw) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN loss_rate_raw IN ('NaN', 'INF', '-INF', '+INF') THEN NULL
    WHEN CAST(loss_rate_raw AS REAL) IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN (CAST(loss_rate_raw AS REAL) = 1.0/0.0) THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(loss_rate_raw AS REAL)
  END AS loss_rate
FROM raw_items_with_loss_rate
WHERE
  trim(loss_rate_raw) != ''
  AND loss_rate_raw NOT IN ('NaN', 'INF', '-INF', '+INF')
  AND CAST(loss_rate_raw AS REAL) IS NOT NULL
  AND NOT (CAST(loss_rate_raw AS REAL) = 1.0/0.0)

semantic_filters.loss_rate: IS NOT NULL and IS NUMERIC/FINITE

views.description: Normalize and validate the loss rate values: cast/convert the raw loss rate to a numeric type, drop or mark rows with non-numeric or invalid values (e.g., strings that cannot cast or NaN/Inf). Produce a canonical numeric field loss_rate for downstream aggregates.

views.name: per_item_loss_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  item_code AS item_id,
  AVG("loss_rate_%") AS loss_rate
FROM veg_loss_rate_df
WHERE item_code IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY item_code
views.description: Ensure one row per item with its single canonical loss_rate. If the source can contain multiple rows per item, reduce by selecting the appropriate representative value per item (e.g., average or latest) so downstream steps operate one-row-per-item. Do not compute dataset-wide statistics here.

views.name: veg_whsle_rows_filtered
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  v."index" AS row_id,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', v.whsle_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  c.category_code AS category_id,
  c.category_name AS category_name,
  v."whsle_px_rmb-kg" AS wholesale_price,
  NULL AS selling_price,
  NULL AS loss_amount,
  lr."loss_rate_%" AS loss_rate
FROM veg_whsle_df v
LEFT JOIN veg_cat c
  ON v.item_code = c.item_code
LEFT JOIN veg_loss_rate_df lr
  ON v.item_code = lr.item_code
WHERE CAST(strftime('%Y', v.whsle_date) AS INTEGER) >= 2020
  AND CAST(strftime('%Y', v.whsle_date) AS INTEGER) <= 2023
views.description: Select the raw veg wholesale rows restricted to the target year range (2020-2023). Keep all source numeric and identifier fields needed for later aggregation (wholesale price amount, selling price amount, loss amount, loss rate, category id/name, year, and any row identifier).

views.name: veg_whsle_rows_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  vwr.row_id AS row_id,
  CAST(vwr.year AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CASE
    WHEN vwr.category_id IS NOT NULL THEN CAST(vwr.category_id AS TEXT)
    WHEN vwr.category_name IS NOT NULL THEN vwr.category_name
    ELSE NULL
  END AS category_id,
  CASE
    WHEN vwr.category_name IS NOT NULL THEN vwr.category_name
    WHEN vwr.category_id IS NOT NULL THEN CAST(vwr.category_id AS TEXT)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS category_name,
  CASE
    WHEN vwr.wholesale_price IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(vwr.wholesale_price AS REAL)
  END AS wholesale_price,
  CASE
    WHEN vwr.selling_price IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(vwr.selling_price AS REAL)
  END AS selling_price,
  CASE
    WHEN vwr.loss_amount IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(vwr.loss_amount AS REAL)
  END AS loss_amount,
  -- Normalize loss_rate to decimal fraction (e.g. 0.05 for 5). Input may be a percentage like 5 or a fraction like 0.05.
  CASE
    WHEN vwr.loss_rate IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN ABS(CAST(vwr.loss_rate AS REAL)) > 1.0 THEN CAST(vwr.loss_rate AS REAL) / 100.0
    ELSE CAST(vwr.loss_rate AS REAL)
  END AS loss_rate_normalized
FROM veg_whsle_rows_filtered vwr
views.description: Normalize and clean the filtered rows: cast numeric fields to consistent numeric types, canonicalize category identifier/name (fill/choose missing name from id or vice versa), and normalize loss_rate representation to a consistent decimal fraction or percentage as used in the data. Preserve one row per original row.

views.name: grouped_financial_metrics_raw
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(strftime('%Y', vw.whsle_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  vc.category_code AS category_id,
  vc.category_name AS category_name,
  AVG(vw."whsle_px_rmb-kg") AS avg_wholesale_price_raw,
  MAX(vw."whsle_px_rmb-kg") AS max_wholesale_price_raw,
  MIN(vw."whsle_px_rmb-kg") AS min_wholesale_price_raw,
  SUM(vw."whsle_px_rmb-kg") AS sum_wholesale_price_raw,
  -- sum of selling price per available join from transactions: compute total selling amount matching item_code and year
  (
    SELECT COALESCE(SUM(tx."unit_selling_px_rmb/kg" * tx."qty_sold(kg)"), 0.0)
    FROM veg_txn_df tx
    WHERE tx.item_code = vw.item_code
      AND CAST(strftime('%Y', tx.txn_date) AS INTEGER) = CAST(strftime('%Y', vw.whsle_date) AS INTEGER)
  ) AS sum_selling_price_raw,
  -- average loss rate per category-year from veg_loss_rate_df joined by item_code
  (
    SELECT AVG(lr."loss_rate_%")
    FROM veg_loss_rate_df lr
    WHERE lr.item_code = vw.item_code
  ) AS avg_loss_rate_raw,
  -- sum loss amount: for rows where loss_rate is available, compute wholesale_price * loss_rate% / 100 summed per category-year
  (
    SELECT COALESCE(SUM(vw2."whsle_px_rmb-kg" * COALESCE(lr2."loss_rate_%", 0.0) / 100.0), 0.0)
    FROM veg_whsle_df vw2
    LEFT JOIN veg_loss_rate_df lr2 ON lr2.item_code = vw2.item_code
    WHERE vc.category_code = (
      SELECT vc2.category_code FROM veg_cat vc2 WHERE vc2.item_code = vw2.item_code LIMIT 1
    )
      AND CAST(strftime('%Y', vw2.whsle_date) AS INTEGER) = CAST(strftime('%Y', vw.whsle_date) AS INTEGER)
  ) AS sum_loss_amount_raw,
  COUNT(*) AS row_count
FROM veg_whsle_df vw
LEFT JOIN veg_cat vc ON vc.item_code = vw.item_code
GROUP BY CAST(strftime('%Y', vw.whsle_date) AS INTEGER), vc.category_code, vc.category_name
views.description: Aggregate normalized rows by year and category to compute the raw grouped measures needed for final metrics: average wholesale price, max/min wholesale price, sum wholesale price, sum selling price, average loss rate, sum loss amount, and counts needed for averages. Do not round values here; keep numeric precision.

views.name: grouped_financial_metrics_final
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  gfmr.year AS year,
  gfmr.category_id AS category_id,
  gfmr.category_name AS category_name,
  ROUND(gfmr.avg_wholesale_price_raw, 2) AS average_wholesale_price,
  ROUND(gfmr.max_wholesale_price_raw, 2) AS maximum_wholesale_price,
  ROUND(gfmr.min_wholesale_price_raw, 2) AS minimum_wholesale_price,
  ROUND(gfmr.max_wholesale_price_raw - gfmr.min_wholesale_price_raw, 2) AS wholesale_price_difference,
  ROUND(gfmr.sum_wholesale_price_raw, 2) AS total_wholesale_price,
  ROUND(gfmr.sum_selling_price_raw, 2) AS total_selling_price,
  ROUND(gfmr.avg_loss_rate_raw, 2) AS average_loss_rate,
  ROUND(gfmr.sum_loss_amount_raw, 2) AS total_loss,
  ROUND((gfmr.sum_selling_price_raw - gfmr.sum_wholesale_price_raw - gfmr.sum_loss_amount_raw), 2) AS profit
FROM grouped_financial_metrics_raw gfmr
views.description: Compute derived metrics and format results for presentation: wholesale_price_difference (max - min), profit (total_selling_price - total_wholesale_price - total_loss), and round all numeric outputs to two decimals. Keep one row per year and category and apply ordering by year ascending then category ascending in the final query layer.

views.name: year_period_boundaries
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  year AS year,
  -- canonical Jun-15 date for the year in ISO YYYY-MM-DD format
  printf('%04d-06-15', year) AS jun15_date,
  -- 28-day pre-period: start = Jun15 - 28 days, end = Jun15 - 1 day
  date(printf('%04d-06-15', year), '-28 days') AS pre_period_start_date,
  date(printf('%04d-06-15', year), '-1 day') AS pre_period_end_date,
  -- 28-day post-period: start = Jun15 + 1 day, end = Jun15 + 28 days
  date(printf('%04d-06-15', year), '+1 day') AS post_period_start_date,
  date(printf('%04d-06-15', year), '+28 days') AS post_period_end_date
FROM (
  -- derive distinct years present across all date-bearing tables in the schema
  SELECT DISTINCT cast(strftime('%Y', week_date) AS INTEGER) AS year FROM weekly_sales WHERE week_date IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT cast(strftime('%Y', start_date) AS INTEGER) FROM shopping_cart_users WHERE start_date IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT cast(strftime('%Y', market_date) AS INTEGER) FROM bitcoin_prices WHERE market_date IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT cast(strftime('%Y', txn_date) AS INTEGER) FROM bitcoin_transactions WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT cast(strftime('%Y', txn_date) AS INTEGER) FROM customer_transactions WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT cast(strftime('%Y', start_date) AS INTEGER) FROM customer_nodes WHERE start_date IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT cast(strftime('%Y', end_date) AS INTEGER) FROM customer_nodes WHERE end_date IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT cast(strftime('%Y', week_date_formatted) AS INTEGER) FROM cleaned_weekly_sales WHERE week_date_formatted IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT cast(strftime('%Y', txn_date) AS INTEGER) FROM veg_txn_df WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT cast(strftime('%Y', whsle_date) AS INTEGER) FROM veg_whsle_df WHERE whsle_date IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT cast(strftime('%Y', start_date) AS INTEGER) FROM shopping_cart_campaign_identifier WHERE start_date IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT DISTINCT cast(strftime('%Y', end_date) AS INTEGER) FROM shopping_cart_campaign_identifier WHERE end_date IS NOT NULL
) years
WHERE year IS NOT NULL
views.description: For each calendar year of interest, produce the canonical Jun-15 date and the start and end dates for the 28-day pre-Jun-15 period and the 28-day post-Jun-15 period. Do not apply year filter here (filtering applied later).

views.name: weekly_sales_in_periods
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  yb.year AS year,
  CASE
    WHEN date(substr(ws.week_date, 7, 2) || '-' || substr(ws.week_date, 4, 2) || '-' || substr(ws.week_date, 1, 2)) BETWEEN yb.pre_period_start_date AND yb.pre_period_end_date THEN 'pre'
    WHEN date(substr(ws.week_date, 7, 2) || '-' || substr(ws.week_date, 4, 2) || '-' || substr(ws.week_date, 1, 2)) BETWEEN yb.post_period_start_date AND yb.post_period_end_date THEN 'post'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS period_label,
  -- normalize week_date to ISO-like YYYY-MM-DD where possible by converting from d/m/yy
  date(substr(ws.week_date, 7, 2) || '-' || substr(ws.week_date, 4, 2) || '-' || substr(ws.week_date, 1, 2)) AS week_date,
  ws.sales AS weekly_sales_value,
  rowid AS weekly_sales_row_id
FROM weekly_sales ws
JOIN year_period_boundaries yb
  ON 1=1
WHERE
  -- only keep rows that fall into either pre or post period for some year
  (date(substr(ws.week_date, 7, 2) || '-' || substr(ws.week_date, 4, 2) || '-' || substr(ws.week_date, 1, 2)) BETWEEN yb.pre_period_start_date AND yb.pre_period_end_date
   OR date(substr(ws.week_date, 7, 2) || '-' || substr(ws.week_date, 4, 2) || '-' || substr(ws.week_date, 1, 2)) BETWEEN yb.post_period_start_date AND yb.post_period_end_date)
views.description: Select weekly-sales rows whose week date falls within any period defined by year_period_boundaries and attach the corresponding year and which period the row falls into (pre or post). Each row corresponds to one weekly-sales record assigned to at most one period for a specific year.

views.name: period_sales_aggregates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  year,
  period_label,
  SUM(weekly_sales_value) AS period_total_sales
FROM weekly_sales_in_periods
GROUP BY year, period_label
views.description: Aggregate weekly_sales_in_periods to compute total sales per year and period (sum of weekly_sales_value). One row per year-period (pre or post).

views.name: yearly_pre_post_comparison
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  yb.year AS year,
  yb.pre_period_start_date AS pre_period_start_date,
  yb.pre_period_end_date AS pre_period_end_date,
  psa_pre.period_total_sales AS pre_period_total_sales,
  yb.post_period_start_date AS post_period_start_date,
  yb.post_period_end_date AS post_period_end_date,
  psa_post.period_total_sales AS post_period_total_sales,
  CASE
    WHEN psa_pre.period_total_sales IS NULL OR psa_pre.period_total_sales = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE ((psa_post.period_total_sales - psa_pre.period_total_sales) * 100.0) / psa_pre.period_total_sales
  END AS pct_change
FROM year_period_boundaries yb
LEFT JOIN period_sales_aggregates psa_pre
  ON psa_pre.year = yb.year
  AND psa_pre.period_label = 'pre'
LEFT JOIN period_sales_aggregates psa_post
  ON psa_post.year = yb.year
  AND psa_post.period_label = 'post'
views.description: Combine the period_sales_aggregates with year_period_boundaries to produce one row per year containing the pre- and post-period start/end dates, the two period total sales, and the percent change ((post - pre) / pre * 100). Handle division-by-zero by yielding NULL for pct_change when pre period total is zero. Apply filter to include only years 2018, 2019, 2020 and order by year ascending in the final query.

views.name: sales_pre_post_periods_sel
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  rowid AS sale_id,
  week_date AS sale_date,
  sales AS sales_amount,
  CASE
    WHEN date(week_date) BETWEEN date('2020-06-15', '-12 weeks') AND date('2020-06-14') THEN 'pre'
    WHEN date(week_date) BETWEEN date('2020-06-15') AND date('2020-06-15', '+11 weeks') THEN 'post'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS period_flag,
  region,
  platform,
  age_band,
  demographic,
  customer_type
FROM cleaned_weekly_sales
WHERE date(week_date) BETWEEN date('2020-06-15', '-12 weeks') AND date('2020-06-15', '+11 weeks')

semantic_filters.date_boundary: split by pre-period (12 weeks ending day before 2020-06-15) vs post-period (12 weeks starting 2020-06-15); include only rows whose sale_date falls in those intervals

views.description: Select sales records that fall in either the pre-period (the 12 weeks ending the day before the boundary date) or the post-period (the 12 weeks starting on the boundary date). Mark each row as belonging to pre or post period. Retain the sales measure and all attribute value columns for region, platform, age band, demographic, and customer type.

views.name: attribute_value_pct_change_norm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  aggregated.attribute_type AS attribute_type,
  aggregated.attribute_value AS attribute_value,
  COALESCE(pre.period_total, 0) AS pre_period_sales,
  COALESCE(post.period_total, 0) AS post_period_sales,
  CASE
    WHEN pre.period_total IS NULL AND post.period_total IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN pre.period_total = 0 AND post.period_total = 0 THEN 0.0
    WHEN pre.period_total = 0 AND post.period_total <> 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE ( (CAST(post.period_total AS REAL) - CAST(pre.period_total AS REAL)) / CAST(pre.period_total AS REAL) ) * 100.0
  END AS percentage_change,
  CASE
    WHEN pre.period_total IS NULL AND post.period_total IS NULL THEN 1
    WHEN pre.period_total = 0 AND post.period_total <> 0 THEN 1
    WHEN pre.period_total IS NULL OR post.period_total IS NULL THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS is_infinite_or_undefined
FROM (
  SELECT attribute_type, attribute_value
  FROM (
    SELECT 'region' AS attribute_type, region AS attribute_value FROM sales_pre_post_periods_sel
    UNION
    SELECT 'platform' AS attribute_type, platform AS attribute_value FROM sales_pre_post_periods_sel
    UNION
    SELECT 'age_band' AS attribute_type, age_band AS attribute_value FROM sales_pre_post_periods_sel
    UNION
    SELECT 'demographic' AS attribute_type, demographic AS attribute_value FROM sales_pre_post_periods_sel
    UNION
    SELECT 'customer_type' AS attribute_type, customer_type AS attribute_value FROM sales_pre_post_periods_sel
  )
  WHERE attribute_value IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY attribute_type, attribute_value
) AS aggregated
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    period_flag,
    region,
    platform,
    age_band,
    demographic,
    customer_type,
    SUM(sales_amount) AS period_total
  FROM sales_pre_post_periods_sel
  WHERE period_flag = 'pre'
  GROUP BY region, platform, age_band, demographic, customer_type, period_flag
) AS pre
ON (
  (aggregated.attribute_type = 'region' AND pre.region = aggregated.attribute_value)
  OR (aggregated.attribute_type = 'platform' AND pre.platform = aggregated.attribute_value)
  OR (aggregated.attribute_type = 'age_band' AND pre.age_band = aggregated.attribute_value)
  OR (aggregated.attribute_type = 'demographic' AND pre.demographic = aggregated.attribute_value)
  OR (aggregated.attribute_type = 'customer_type' AND pre.customer_type = aggregated.attribute_value)
)
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    period_flag,
    region,
    platform,
    age_band,
    demographic,
    customer_type,
    SUM(sales_amount) AS period_total
  FROM sales_pre_post_periods_sel
  WHERE period_flag = 'post'
  GROUP BY region, platform, age_band, demographic, customer_type, period_flag
) AS post
ON (
  (aggregated.attribute_type = 'region' AND post.region = aggregated.attribute_value)
  OR (aggregated.attribute_type = 'platform' AND post.platform = aggregated.attribute_value)
  OR (aggregated.attribute_type = 'age_band' AND post.age_band = aggregated.attribute_value)
  OR (aggregated.attribute_type = 'demographic' AND post.demographic = aggregated.attribute_value)
  OR (aggregated.attribute_type = 'customer_type' AND post.customer_type = aggregated.attribute_value)
)
views.description: Normalize and compute the percentage change per attribute_type/attribute_value by joining the pre and post period totals. Compute percentage_change = (post - pre) / NULL-safe(pre) * 100. Apply rules for pre_period_sales = 0: mark infinite/undefined cases and set pct_change accordingly (finite or sentinel). Retain a flag for excluded/infinite values for later averaging decisions.

views.name: attribute_type_average_pct_change_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  av.attribute_type AS attribute_type,
  AVG(av.percentage_change) AS average_percentage_change_in_sales,
  SUM(CASE WHEN av.is_infinite_or_undefined = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS attribute_value_count_included,
  SUM(CASE WHEN av.is_infinite_or_undefined != 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS attribute_value_count_excluded
FROM attribute_value_pct_change_norm av
GROUP BY av.attribute_type
views.description: For each attribute_type, compute the average of percentage_change across its attribute_values, excluding values flagged as infinite/undefined. Also produce a count of excluded values so consumers can see how many were omitted.
